video_title: How Does LeBron Fit Into the 76ers Dynamic? | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' fit and buy-in with the Philadelphia 76ers
quotes.excerpt: I don't know how much buy-in he has from everybody else on that roster.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Your thoughts on LeBron signing with Philly?

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I was as surprised as everyone else. I thought Philadelphia was in last place of the options he was looking at. Either it's going to work spectacularly or it's going to be a failure. I don't know how much buy-in he has from everybody else on that roster. We heard reports of Joel Embiid calling to talk to him and wanting him to come, and certainly Tyrese Maxey, who is a fellow Clutch client and looks up to LeBron. I did not hear of Jalen Brown calling and asking him to come.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Concerns regarding Jalen Brown's buy-in to the LeBron James experiment
quotes.excerpt: If you don't have buy-in from Jalen Brown, it's not going to work.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I saw some reports that he talked to Jalen Brown, but I haven't heard that specifically.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: That's the one that I'm curious how that's going to work, because if you don't have buy-in from Jalen Brown, it's not going to work. This whole experiment is not going to work. Hopefully they talked in a way that Jalen Brown is comfortable with. That's going to be the whole thing, right? Joel Embiid's health is Joel Embiid's health. If Joel is there, great. If he's not there, they'll figure out how to do it without him. That's been the case for so many years in Philly, it's almost status quo.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James prioritizing winning a championship with the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: He seemed to make this purely for basketball reasons.
quotes.quote: Did it surprise you that he prioritized winning another championship? He used that word in his statement: winning a championship, bringing a championship to Philadelphia. There were a lot of potential reasons he could have made a decision. He could have made a decision based on family, staying on the West Coast, gone to Golden State, nostalgia, go back to Cleveland, even to Miami. But he seemed to make this purely for basketball reasons. It was not, as he wrote, about his family. It was not about money, two-year, $8 million deal.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' decision to join the 76ers makes sense
quotes.excerpt: I think it makes sense what he is doing.
quotes.quote: I think it makes sense what he is doing. What he would have done in Cleveland or Miami kind of is this murky middle ground. The Warriors would have made sense to me, and this makes sense to me. The Cleveland and Miami, actually, even though I know for a lot of people those were the favorites, that would have made less sense to me because I think neither team would have been a favorite, maybe even to be in the top two or three in the East, had he picked one of those teams. And in Philly at least, if it works, again, if it works, they have the chance to be a huge powerhouse.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' motivation to play for something again
quotes.excerpt: It felt really great to play for something again.
quotes.quote: I was at the Paris Olympics, and one of the things that really struck me that he said after they won was, 'It felt really great to play for something again.' And he said it again when he got back and gave his introductory press conference for his first time back with the Lakers after winning the gold medal. He said it a second time: 'It felt really great to play for something again.' Look, this is a guy who, from the time he got into the league until 2020, was in the NBA Finals 10 times. In the last six years, since 2020, he has been in the NBA Finals zero times. That is a huge swing.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James transitioning to a point guard role
quotes.excerpt: LeBron is going to play point guard.
quotes.quote: You've got on paper one of the most dynamic offensive teams, at least in the Eastern Conference, probably in the entire NBA. LeBron, and look, some of the reporting now is out there, LeBron is going to play point guard. The suggestion in him playing point guard is that he is going to see his offensive numbers go way down. He is going to focus on being a distributor, which he has to be on that team. They have four players that were top 50 in usage rate last season. Jalen Brunson had the highest usage rate of his career, Tyrese Maxey is a budding superstar.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Joel Embiid's dominance and team hierarchy
quotes.excerpt: When Joel Embiid is on the floor, Joel Embiid is going to believe it's his team.
quotes.quote: I had one coach say to me, 'When Joel Embiid is on the floor, Joel Embiid is going to believe it's his team.' Joel Embiid is going to say, 'I'm getting my 20 shots, I'm standing there in the middle, I'm doing things my way.' It is critical for LeBron to take on this approach and be the point forward, which he knew coming in.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' innate floor vision and playmaking
quotes.excerpt: He has an innate sense of the floor, he is fantastic at seeing the court.
quotes.quote: He knows the sacrifice. He made this decision. He knows what he is doing. He is buying in by definition of being on this team. We know that he is. And by the way, it's a great role for him. He has an innate sense of the floor, he is fantastic at seeing the court. He knows players are developing before they develop. He is a terrific passer, and it is something that has been baked into him since high school, that being the guy who helps the scorer is just as important as being the guy who scores.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of the mid-season stretch for team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: That stretch of games between December 26th and February 5th, that's when you really find out.
quotes.quote: It's when you get to post-Christmas and before the trade deadline. That stretch of games between December 26th and February 5th, that's when you really find out the character of a team because when you're coming off a three-game road trip through like Denver, Oklahoma City, and San Antonio, and you're trudging back to frozen Philadelphia at 3:00 in the morning off a three-game road trip, or whatever it may be, that's when you're going to find out if you're really all on board.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The benefits of the Eastern Conference for LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: The travel is going to be a lot easier.
quotes.quote: Going back East does a lot of things for LeBron. I actually think the Eastern Conference is one of the most talent-rich it's been in a very long time. The travel is going to be a lot easier. That is not a small thing when you are that age and your body needs more sleep and recovery time. The number of games that you're just going, hopping up to New York, hopping up to Brooklyn, hopping down to Washington D.C., hopping down to Charlotte, it's a big difference than getting on a plane.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' impact on NBA television ratings
quotes.excerpt: NBA TV ratings are going to go up next year because LeBron made this decision.
quotes.quote: NBA TV ratings are going to go up next year because LeBron made this decision. And I think there was a real confusion when LeBron left Cleveland for Los Angeles and people were saying, 'Oh man, the TV ratings, LeBron's going to the Lakers, that's just going to be an explosion of TV ratings.' It actually hurt the NBA because the Lakers already drew television ratings, especially in the Western markets where people are awake and they were already going to draw. LeBron drew television ratings in Cleveland and in the Eastern markets where people liked watching him play at 7:00 p.m. Eastern.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The potential for a disastrous 76ers season
quotes.excerpt: You're under 500 with the Sixers ever trade LeBron.
quotes.quote: Do you think there's any chance the most hilarious thing in NBA history could happen, which is you get to January, everybody hates each other, there's like a big injury or two mixed in there, you're under 500 with the Sixers ever trade LeBron? He's now the most tradable guy. He's as tradable as anybody. He's making 4 million bucks.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' potential retirement
quotes.excerpt: He could always just retire though.
quotes.quote: I mean, he could always just retire though.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The risk of the 76ers team collapsing
quotes.excerpt: This team just craters.
quotes.quote: This team just craters, which is again, I think it's going to be fine. I think they'll be pretty good, not great. I think every history suggests that with very few exceptions, it takes time to meld a team like this together. You not only have one new star, you have two new stars. Guys that demand the ball, there are going to be bumps along the road.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse's coaching challenge with the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: We'll see what Nick Nurse has got.
quotes.quote: We'll see what Nick Nurse has got. Remember, Nick Nurse was on just as shaky ground as Daryl Morey was, you know, just a couple of months ago. Well, I mean, some of that was his fault too. They haven't they haven't won. They haven't achieved.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse's performance under difficult circumstances
quotes.excerpt: He has done as good a job with what he has been given as it was possible.
quotes.quote: He has done as good a job with what he has been given as it was possible to do. Look over the list of calamities that man has had to like stand guard and captain over. Paul George is suspended for 25 games. Nick Nurse didn't get into a fight with James Harden either. So, you know, there's I actually think Nick is a great coach for this situation. He's a championship coach, he's creative, he's obviously he's done what they're trying to do. He understands how to deal with superstars who are not conventional.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Nurse's experience managing superstars
quotes.excerpt: Having to manage Kawhi Leonard in Toronto that year was no small thing.
quotes.quote: Having to manage Kawhi Leonard in Toronto that year was no small thing. I watched it up close. There were a lot of personalities in that team too, Kyle Lowry is his own personality. So, I think he is going to be good with dealing with a lot of these factors, but in the end, it's going to be up to the players and how much and how they want to work together and then a lot of it's going to be luck too.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' veteran minimum contract
quotes.excerpt: It's a veteran exception, 4 million. He's making the shit under 4 million this year.
quotes.quote: Basically, it's a veteran exception, 4 million. He's making the shit under 4 million this year. He's making whatever. He's making the shit under 4 million this year, yeah. Is on the heels of Victor Wembanyama taking the less money that he could have taken. Donovan Mitchell going for the earlier contract the same way that Jalen Brunson did, which is quote, leaving 100 million on the table, even though you get then get that back on your next contract if you make it to your next contract.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The shift in NBA player compensation and decision-making
quotes.excerpt: Can you start making decisions that have nothing to do with money?
quotes.quote: Now the amount of money has gotten so great. There are definitely still guys who go broke. We see it, we see the documentaries, the 30 for 30s, whatever. But the money is so much greater now, the endorsement money is greater, the salary is greater, the minimums are greater, that you just have a much bigger cushion. And the guys who are bigger stars and take care of their money have an enormous cushion. And when the Supermax came in, I remember very clearly looking at Tracy McGrady on the show we did on ESPN and saying, 'How much money is enough that you can start making decisions that have nothing to do with money?'

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the Supermax on team development
quotes.excerpt: If you go what Wemby did, say 25%, that changes the way you can develop your team.
quotes.quote: It's really all about the Supermax guys, the guys that are in the 35% tax bracket. If you go what Wemby did, say 25%, that changes the way you can develop your team. Down the line, you can probably find a way to keep both Steph Curry and Dylan Harper on your team if you're willing to take that. And look, I'm for that too, because again, for all the reasons you just kind of articulated there, like how much money is enough? How much do you need at this point? How many hundreds of millions of dollars are going to make a difference?
